Sodium fluoride is a corrosive compound that, when ingested in toxic amounts, causes severe irritation to the mucous membranes and the digestive tract. The primary acute effect of sodium fluoride poisoning is a massive irritant effect on the gastrointestinal system, causing symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. This is due to the formation of hydrofluoric acid when sodium fluoride comes into contact with stomach acid.

While sodium fluoride can also cause metabolic disorders (by binding to calcium and affecting enzyme systems) and can have effects on the nervous system, the most immediate and characteristic effect in acute oral poisoning is the severe irritation of mucous membranes and the digestive tract.
